item.title: Quickstart
item.description:
Quickstart#

In this tutorial you install kevin, start an example environment with an nginx container, and reach it over HTTPS through the kevin proxy.

Prerequisites#

  • Docker, running. Podman also works. If both are installed, add --engine podman to each kevin command.

  • git and curl.

  • A clone of the kevin repository, for the example environment:

    git clone https://github.com/justenwalker/kevin.git
cd kevin

item.title: Contributing
item.description:
Contributing#

kevin builds with gnob, vendored under build/. Bootstrap it once. After that, it rebuilds itself when its sources change:

go generate -C ./build -tags gnob . # bootstrap, once
./build/gnob -help # list every target, with a one-line description each
./build/gnob build # build bin/kevin and bin/kevin-plugin-echo
./bin/kevin -C examples/web run # try it, Ctrl-C to remove

Run one test with go test:

go test ./internal/dag/... -run TestName -v
go test -C tests/e2e -tags e2e -run TestName ./... # an end-to-end test: tests/e2e is its own Go module

golangci-lint (.golangci.yaml) enables every linter, then disables some. The comments in the file give the reason for each. Read them before you add a //nolint. docs/GO_CONVENTIONS.md covers the style rules that the linter cannot check.

item.title: Kevin vs. Other Tools
item.description:
kevin vs. other tools#

kevin combines four things: an environment that exists only while you use it, a DAG that runs independent steps in parallel, a proxy that terminates TLS, controls egress, and can intercept real hostnames, and a plugin protocol that any language can implement. This page compares kevin with other tools, from the most similar to the least.

Garden#

Garden is the most similar. A Garden project is a graph of actions run by providers, the same model as kevin’s steps and plugins, and it is for the same job: development and test environments, locally or in CI.
